To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the steady-state MSD and MSE curves are no longer monotonically increasing function of the step-size when communication links are noisy.

(a) the steady-state MSD and EMSE are not monotone functions of the step size in a noisy link environment; and (b) the optimal step size that minimizes the steady state MSD, EMSE and MSE in each individual node is given by the closed-form expression in the special case of the proposed adaptive network with noisy links.
the optimal step-size is not a monotonic function of the noise power in the links and the steady-state performance in the nodes is not monotonically decreasing function of the noise variance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the steady-state performance of adaptive networks in which communication links among the nodes are noisy.
the steady-state performance analysis of the LMS adaptive networks in a realistic scenario with noisy links.
a more realistic case where communication links between nodes of adaptive network are noisy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the steady-state MSD is a non-monotonic function of the step-size in each node.
, unlike the ideal link assumption, noisy links can improve the steady-state performance of adaptive networks.
the optimal step-size for noisy links is always smaller than the optimal step-size of ideal links.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the steady-state performance of the incremental LMS adaptive network in the presence of noisy links is not necessarily a monotonically increasing function of the step-size.
the proposed analysis is able to provide closed-form expressions for MSD, EMSE and MSE of the network nodes when links are noisy.

, in addition to providing a more accurate analysis for the performance of incremental LMS adaptive networks, we have also provided a new approach to analyze the steady-state performance of adaptive networks with noisy links.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the steady-state performance of adaptive networks can be improved by carefully choosing the step-size parameter.
the performance of the adaptive network can be improved by using noisy links.
the optimal step-size for the noisy link case is smaller than that for the ideal link case.
